newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says it ready for full NATO integration.
newsitem.headline: Spain says it ready for full NATO integration.

text.p: Spain is likely to announce its readiness to join NATO's military command when alliance leaders meet in Madrid next week for an expansion summit, Defence Minister Eduardo Serra said on Monday.

In contrast to France which has said the time is not right to join NATO's military command, Serra said Madrid's key demands for integration had been met and Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar would probably reaffirm Spain's intention to become a full participant during the summit.

"Everything which Spain thought was an essential condition is being met," Serra told Reuters. "Spain can announce its willingness or readiness to be a full member of the alliance and perhaps this is possible in Madrid."

The leaders of the 16 NATO nations will discuss reorganising the command structure at the July 8-9 summit but no agreement is expected due to outstanding differences between some members. The alliance is also expected to decide to admit several new members from eastern Europe.

Spain's parliament approved full integration into NATO last November. The government then began negotiations, demanding a sub-regional Iberian command covering all Spanish territory including the Canary islands, an Atlantic archepelago now under NATO's Atlantic command.
Spain also insisted on controlling access to the Mediterranean through the Straits of Gibraltar.
"Nobody disputes that Spain must have a sub-regional command with all national territory including the Canary islands under the responsibility of this command," Serra said.
He said Spain and NATO were still negotiating the control over the waters between the Canary islands and Spain, but he expected an acceptable solution to be found.

An agreement on the new NATO command structure is not expected for months, due mainly to differences between Washington and Paris on the southern command and between Greece and Turkey over the eastern Mediterranean.
